recipes.name: Egg white and chorizo breakfast tacos
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 42 g protein, 40 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Brown the chorizo in a pan.
Pour in egg whites and egg, scramble until set.
Warm tortillas on the burner or a dry pan.
Fill and top with pico, hot sauce and cilantro.
recipes.volumeTip: Add a big handful of spinach, peppers and onion to the scramble.

recipes.name: Mango-coconut overnight oats
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 38 g protein, 58 g carbs, 10 g fat

ingredients.name: unsweetened almond or light coconut milk

steps: Stir everything together in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Eat cold. Make 3 or 4 jars at once.

recipes.name: Korean-style egg rice bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 40 g protein, 50 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Heat sesame oil, fry or scramble eggs and whites.
Put rice in a bowl, add eggs and kimchi.
Drizzle soy, crumble seaweed on top.
recipes.volumeTip: Wilt a bag of spinach in the pan first.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt power bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 45 g protein, 45 g carbs, 10 g fat
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl.
Top with berries, granola, honey and cinnamon.

recipes.name: Pollo guisado with rice and beans
recipes.servingSize: 1 portion chicken + 3/4 cup rice + 1/2 cup beans
recipes.nutrition: ~620 cal, 52 g protein, 65 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Season chicken with adobo, brown in oil, set aside.
Soften onion, pepper, garlic and sofrito in the same pot.
Add tomato sauce, sazón, bay leaves, olives, 1 cup water and the chicken.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Portion over rice with beans.
recipes.volumeTip: Serve over a big bed of arugula and spinach with the rice underneath.

recipes.name: Teriyaki chicken and broccoli rice bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~580 cal, 50 g protein, 62 g carbs, 12 g fat
steps: Whisk soy, honey, vinegar, ginger, garlic and cornstarch.
Sear chicken until browned.
Add sauce and simmer until glossy.
Steam broccoli.
Portion rice, chicken and broccoli; top with sesame and scallions.
recipes.volumeTip: Two full cups of broccoli per bowl; swap half the rice for cauliflower rice.

swaps.label: Flank steak
swaps.note: Same sauce.

swaps.label: Pork tenderloin
swaps.note: Same sauce.

recipes.name: Turkey picadillo bowl
recipes.servingSize: 1 portion over 3/4 cup rice or 1 sweet potato
recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 48 g protein, 55 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Brown the turkey.
Add onion, pepper and garlic, cook until soft.
Add tomatoes, raisins, olives, capers and seasonings.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Serve over rice or roasted sweet potato.
recipes.volumeTip: Spoon hot over arugula and spinach so the greens wilt.

recipes.name: Spicy tuna and avocado bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 46 g protein, 52 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Drain tuna, mix with mayo, sriracha and soy.
Put rice in a bowl, add tuna, sliced cucumber and avocado.
Top with ginger, seaweed and sesame. No cooking.
recipes.volumeTip: Double the cucumber and add shredded cabbage.

recipes.name: Mojo pork tenderloin, sweet potatoes, garlicky spinach
recipes.servingSize: about 6 oz pork + 1 sweet potato + spinach
recipes.nutrition: ~600 cal, 55 g protein, 50 g carbs, 18 g fat

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for the marinade + 1 tbsp for the potatoes

steps: Blend citrus juice, 6 garlic cloves, cumin, oregano, 2 tbsp oil and salt; marinate pork 1 to 24 hours.
Cube sweet potatoes, toss with 1 tbsp oil, roast at 425°F for 25 minutes.
Sear pork, then roast to 145°F inside, about 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Wilt spinach with 2 garlic cloves in 1 tsp oil.
Slice pork and serve.

recipes.name: Thai basil chicken with jasmine rice
recipes.nutrition: ~580 cal, 52 g protein, 58 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Stir-fry garlic and chili 30 seconds.
Add chicken and onion, brown well.
Add green beans and the sauces and sugar, cook 3 minutes.
Stir in basil off the heat.
Serve over rice, fried egg on top if wanted.
recipes.volumeTip: Double the green beans, add zucchini, rice on the side.

recipes.name: Jerk salmon with rice and peas and mango salsa
recipes.nutrition: ~620 cal, 48 g protein, 52 g carbs, 24 g fat
steps: Rub salmon with jerk seasoning.
Cook rice in coconut milk plus water with beans, scallion, thyme and allspice.
Bake salmon at 400°F for 12 to 14 minutes.
Dice mango, onion, jalapeño and cilantro, add lime juice.
Plate with salsa on top.

recipes.name: Lean beef bulgogi with kimchi and rice
recipes.nutrition: ~610 cal, 50 g protein, 55 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Freeze the beef 30 minutes, slice thin.
Grate pear, mix with soy, sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and scallions; marinate 1 hour or more.
Sear in a very hot pan in batches.
Steam the greens.
Serve with rice and kimchi.
recipes.volumeTip: Half rice, half cauliflower rice, with cucumber, carrot and radish on the side.

recipes.name: Smash-burger bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~580 cal, 48 g protein, 45 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Cut potato into wedges, roast at 425°F for 25 minutes.
Form beef into 2 balls, smash flat in a very hot pan, salt, cook 2 minutes a side.
Mix mayo, ketchup, mustard and a splash of pickle juice.
Pile greens, tomato, onion and pickles in a bowl, add patties, wedges and sauce.

recipes.name: Slow-cooker ropa vieja
recipes.nutrition: ~590 cal, 54 g protein, 55 g carbs, 15 g fat
steps: Put everything except olives, rice and lime in the slow cooker.
Cook on low 8 hours.
Shred the beef with two forks, stir in olives.
Serve with rice or boiled yuca and a lime wedge.

recipes.name: Sheet-pan fajita chicken with black beans
recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 52 g protein, 50 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Slice chicken, pepper and onion, toss with oil and seasoning.
Roast on a sheet pan at 425°F for 18 minutes.
Warm the beans.
Build tacos or a bowl with salsa and avocado.
recipes.volumeTip: Use a shredded cabbage base and eat it as a huge bowl.

swaps.label: Flank or skirt steak
swaps.note: Roast 10–12 minutes.

recipes.name: Lighter sancocho-style chicken soup
recipes.servingSize: 1 big bowl with one piece of starch
steps: Simmer chicken in broth with sofrito 20 minutes.
Add yuca, calabaza, corn and carrots, cook 20 minutes.
Add cabbage and celery, cook 10 minutes.
Shred chicken back in, finish with cilantro and lime.

swaps.label: Beef stew meat
swaps.note: Simmer the beef 60 minutes before the vegetables.

recipes.name: Ginger chicken and vegetable soup
steps: Simmer broth with ginger and garlic.
Poach chicken 15 minutes, remove and shred.
Add mushrooms and cabbage 5 minutes, bok choy 2 minutes.
Return chicken, add soy, sesame oil and scallions.

swaps.label: Pork loin
swaps.note: Poach 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Caldo de pollo
steps: Simmer chicken in broth 20 minutes, remove and shred.
Add rice, carrots, chayote and tomato, cook 12 minutes.
Add zucchini and cabbage, cook 8 minutes.
Return chicken, finish with cilantro and lime.

swaps.label: Caldo de res (beef)
swaps.note: Caldo de res: simmer the beef 90 minutes first.

recipes.name: Protein egg drop soup
steps: Simmer broth with ginger and soy.
Add spinach.
Beat egg whites and egg, pour in slowly while stirring.
Top with scallion. Ready in 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Carne guisada (Caribbean beef stew)
recipes.nutrition: ~610 cal, 50 g protein, 60 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Season beef with adobo, brown in oil in batches.
Soften onion, pepper, garlic and sofrito in the same pot.
Add tomato sauce, sazón, oregano, bay leaves, broth and beef.
Cover and simmer 60 minutes.
Add potatoes, carrots and olives, simmer 25 minutes until tender.
Serve over rice.

recipes.name: Korean ground beef bowls
recipes.nutrition: ~620 cal, 50 g protein, 55 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Brown the beef, drain any fat.
Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in soy, sugar, sesame oil and gochujang, simmer 3 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in a separate pan.
Portion rice, beef, spinach, cucumber and carrot; top with scallions and sesame.

recipes.name: Pork al pastor bowls
recipes.servingSize: 1 bowl with 3/4 cup rice and 1/4 cup beans, or 3 tacos
recipes.nutrition: ~590 cal, 54 g protein, 65 g carbs, 10 g fat
steps: Blend chipotles, sauce, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano and achiote.
Marinate pork 1 to 24 hours.
Sear pork in a very hot pan in batches until charred at the edges.
Char pineapple chunks and sliced onion in the same pan.
Serve over rice and beans or in tortillas with cilantro and lime.

recipes.name: Lemongrass pork noodle bowls (Vietnamese-style)
recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 52 g protein, 58 g carbs, 11 g fat
steps: Mix lemongrass, garlic, shallot, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, soy and oil; marinate pork 30 minutes or more.
Shred carrots, toss with vinegar and a pinch of sugar.
Cook noodles, rinse cold.
Sear pork in a hot pan until browned.
Stir 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, lime juice, chili and 3 tbsp water for the dressing.
Build bowls: noodles, pork, cucumber, carrot, herbs, dressing.

recipes.name: Slow-cooker pernil-style pork
recipes.servingSize: about 6 oz pork + 3/4 cup rice with pigeon peas
recipes.nutrition: ~640 cal, 48 g protein, 50 g carbs, 26 g fat
steps: Mash garlic with oregano, adobo, sazón, oil and the juices.
Cut slits in the pork, rub the paste in, rest overnight if possible.
Slow cook on low 8 hours.
Shred, spread on a sheet pan and broil 4 minutes to crisp the edges.
Cook rice with sofrito and pigeon peas.
Serve pork over the rice with a spoon of the cooking juices.

recipes.name: Spicy pork bulgogi
recipes.nutrition: ~590 cal, 54 g protein, 58 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Mix gochujang, chili flakes, soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger.
Toss with pork and sliced onion, marinate 30 minutes or more.
Stir-fry in a very hot pan in batches until the edges caramelize.
Add sliced cabbage for the last 2 minutes.
Serve over rice with scallions and kimchi.

recipes.name: Beef and broccoli
recipes.nutrition: ~610 cal, 55 g protein, 55 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Toss beef with 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy, rest 15 minutes.
Whisk the remaining soy, oyster sauce, sugar, broth and 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Steam broccoli until just tender.
Sear beef in batches in a very hot pan, 1 minute a side.
Add garlic and ginger, pour in the sauce, simmer until glossy.
Fold in broccoli and sesame oil, serve over rice.

recipes.name: Bistec encebollado (steak and onions)
recipes.nutrition: ~600 cal, 54 g protein, 55 g carbs, 16 g fat

ingredients.name: thin-sliced top round or cube steak

steps: Marinate steak with vinegar, garlic, oregano, sazón, adobo and half the onions for 1 hour or overnight.
Sear steak in oil, 1 to 2 minutes a side, set aside.
Cook all the onions in the same pan until soft.
Return steak with the marinade and broth, cover and simmer 20 minutes until tender.
Serve with rice and beans.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt cup
recipes.nutrition: Snack guide: about 15–20 g protein

recipes.name: Protein shake
recipes.nutrition: Snack guide: about 15–20 g protein

recipes.name: String cheese and fruit
recipes.servingSize: 2 sticks and a piece of fruit
recipes.nutrition: Snack guide: about 15–20 g protein

recipes.name: Jerky
recipes.nutrition: Snack guide: about 15–20 g protein

recipes.name: Veggie scramble on toast
recipes.servingSize: 2 eggs and whites on 2 slices of toast
recipes.nutrition: ~440 cal, 35 g protein, 37 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook the diced pepper and onion for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Beat the eggs with the egg whites, pour in, and stir gently until just set, about 2 minutes.
Season, pile onto toast and add hot sauce.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese berry bowl
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 31 g protein, 58 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Top with the berries, granola and chia seeds.
Drizzle with honey.

recipes.name: Peanut butter banana oats
recipes.nutrition: ~580 cal, 42 g protein, 73 g carbs, 15 g fat
steps: Simmer the oats in the milk for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring (or microwave for 2 minutes).
Take off the heat and stir in the protein powder. Add a splash of milk if it's thick.
Top with sliced banana, peanut butter and cinnamon.

recipes.name: Turkey and egg breakfast burritos
recipes.nutrition: ~500 cal, 35 g protein, 44 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Brown the turkey with the cumin and chili powder until no pink remains (165°F).
Add the diced pepper and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Push everything aside and scramble the eggs in the same pan. Stir in the beans.
Divide among the tortillas with the cheese and salsa, and roll up.
Wrap extras in foil. Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze; reheat until hot all the way through.

recipes.name: Banana oat protein pancakes
recipes.nutrition: ~620 cal, 44 g protein, 73 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: Blend the banana, eggs, oats, protein powder, baking powder and cinnamon until smooth.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium-low heat with a little oil.
Pour 3 small pancakes. Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles form, flip, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Top with the berries and honey.

recipes.name: Smoked salmon avocado toast
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 38 g protein, 35 g carbs, 26 g fat
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, salt and pepper, and spread it on the toast.
Fry or poach the eggs.
Top the toast with the smoked salmon, then the eggs and a few capers.

recipes.name: Tofu scramble with black beans
recipes.nutrition: ~620 cal, 39 g protein, 70 g carbs, 21 g fat
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towels and crumble it.
Cook the diced onion and pepper in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the tofu, cumin, turmeric and salt. Cook for 5 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in the beans and spinach until the spinach wilts and everything is hot.
Serve with warm tortillas and salsa.

recipes.name: Chicken burrito bowls
recipes.nutrition: ~600 cal, 50 g protein, 65 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Cook in a hot pan for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and 165°F inside.
Warm the beans and corn.
Divide the rice into 4 containers. Top with the chicken, beans, corn and salsa.
Add avocado, lime and cilantro when serving.
recipes.volumeTip: Serve over a big handful of shredded lettuce and use half the rice.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Brown and crumble instead of cubing; cook to 165°F.

recipes.name: Greek chicken and quinoa bowls
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 51 g protein, 35 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: Marinate the chicken in 1 tbsp oil, the juice of half the lemon, the oregano, minced garlic and salt for 15 minutes.
Simmer the quinoa in 2 cups of water, covered, for 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes a side until 165°F. Rest, then slice.
Dice the cucumber, tomatoes and onion. Toss with the rest of the oil and lemon.
Build the bowls: quinoa, chicken, salad, feta, olives and a spoon of yogurt.

swaps.label: Chickpeas
swaps.note: Warm the chickpeas with the oregano and garlic instead of cooking chicken.

recipes.name: Tuna and white bean salad
recipes.nutrition: ~550 cal, 44 g protein, 56 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the tuna, beans, chopped tomatoes and thinly sliced onion. Toss.
Fold in the spinach.
Serve with toast.

recipes.name: Turkey taco lettuce wraps
recipes.nutrition: ~410 cal, 34 g protein, 27 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Brown the turkey with the diced onion until no pink remains (165°F).
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and heat through.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and top with salsa, avocado, cheese and lime.
recipes.volumeTip: Pile on shredded cabbage and pico de gallo. They add crunch for almost nothing.

recipes.name: Chickpea and spinach curry

ingredients.name: nonfat Greek yogurt
ingredients.note: to serve; leave out for vegan

recipes.nutrition: ~600 cal, 25 g protein, 94 g carbs, 13 g fat
steps: Cook the diced onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, lentils and 1 cup of water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and simmer 5 to 10 minutes more, until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Season with salt and lime juice.
Serve over rice with a spoon of yogurt and cilantro.

recipes.name: Black bean and sweet potato bowls
recipes.nutrition: ~640 cal, 29 g protein, 100 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the sweet potatoes and onion wedges with the oil, chili powder, cumin and salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once.
Simmer the quinoa in 1 1/2 cups of water, covered, for 15 minutes.
Warm the beans.
Build the bowls: quinoa, sweet potato, beans, salsa, avocado, feta, a spoon of yogurt and lime.

recipes.name: Chicken Caesar wraps
recipes.nutrition: ~420 cal, 49 g protein, 28 g carbs, 12 g fat
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Cook in the oil for 5 to 6 minutes a side until 165°F. Rest, then slice.
Stir the yogurt, parmesan, lemon juice, mustard, grated garlic, pepper and a splash of water into a dressing.
Toss the chopped romaine with the dressing.
Fill the tortillas with the lettuce and chicken and roll them tight.
recipes.volumeTip: Use the whole head of romaine and eat the extra as a side salad.

recipes.name: Egg fried rice with vegetables
recipes.nutrition: ~610 cal, 32 g protein, 70 g carbs, 24 g fat
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set and set them aside.
Stir-fry the carrots, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, peas and edamame. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until hot.
Return the eggs. Add the soy sauce, sesame oil and scallions and toss for 1 minute.

swaps.label: Shrimp
swaps.note: Stir-fry the shrimp first until pink, 2 to 3 minutes.

recipes.name: Shrimp and vegetable stir-fry
recipes.nutrition: ~430 cal, 43 g protein, 52 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, cornstarch and 1/4 cup of water.
Stir-fry the broccoli, peppers and mushrooms in the oil over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Set aside.
Cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Return the vegetables, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Finish with the sesame oil and scallions. Serve over rice.

swaps.label: Chicken breast
swaps.note: Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains.

swaps.label: Tofu
swaps.note: Brown the tofu first, 6 to 8 minutes.

recipes.name: Lemon-herb chicken thighs with potatoes and green beans
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 49 g protein, 36 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and salt on a sheet pan. Roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the oil, the lemon zest and juice, garlic, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper.
Add the chicken and green beans to the pan. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Squeeze over more lemon.

recipes.name: Turkey meatballs with marinara and spaghetti
recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 37 g protein, 61 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan.
Mix the turkey, egg, oats, minced garlic, Italian seasoning, half the parmesan and 1/2 tsp salt. Roll into 16 meatballs.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until 165°F inside.
Boil the spaghetti as the packet says, then drain.
Warm the marinara in a pan, wilt in the spinach and add the meatballs.
Serve over the spaghetti with the rest of the parmesan and basil.
recipes.volumeTip: Swap half the spaghetti for roasted zucchini.

recipes.name: Baked cod with lemon, rice and broccoli
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 41 g protein, 69 g carbs, 9 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cook the rice.
Toss the broccoli florets with 1 tbsp oil and salt on a sheet pan. Roast for 10 minutes.
Pat the cod dry. Rub with the rest of the oil, the minced garlic, paprika, salt and pepper.
Add the cod and lemon slices to the pan. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish flakes easily (145°F).
Serve over the rice with lemon.

recipes.name: Shrimp tacos with cabbage slaw
recipes.nutrition: ~420 cal, 43 g protein, 41 g carbs, 12 g fat
steps: Toss the shrimp with the oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Shred the cabbage. Toss with the yogurt, the juice of 1 lime and salt.
Cook the shrimp in a hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Fill with slaw, shrimp, avocado, cilantro and hot sauce. Serve with lime wedges.

swaps.label: Chicken breast
swaps.note: Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains.

recipes.name: Beef and bean chili
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 41 g protein, 46 g carbs, 12 g fat
steps: Brown the beef in a large pot, breaking it up, until no pink remains (160°F). Drain off extra fat.
Add the diced onion and peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and broth. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then. Salt to taste.
Serve with a spoon of yogurt and scallions. Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Cook to 165°F.

recipes.name: Curry-yogurt chicken with rice and cucumber salad
recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 48 g protein, 43 g carbs, 8 g fat
steps: Stir the yogurt, curry powder, ginger, minced garlic, half the lemon juice and salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for 20 minutes (or overnight).
Cook the chicken in the oil in a very hot pan (or under the broiler) for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until charred at the edges and 165°F.
Dice the cucumbers, tomatoes and onion. Toss with the rest of the lemon, salt and cilantro.
Serve the chicken over rice with the salad.

recipes.name: Tofu and vegetable stir-fry
recipes.nutrition: ~530 cal, 29 g protein, 58 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Press the tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes, then cube it.
Brown the tofu in 1 tbsp oil for 6 to 8 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Stir-fry the vegetables in the rest of the oil for 4 to 5 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, cornstarch and 1/4 cup of water. Pour in with the tofu and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.
Finish with the sesame oil, sesame seeds and scallions. Serve over rice.

recipes.name: Turkey-stuffed bell peppers
recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 36 g protein, 47 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Halve the peppers lengthwise, take out the seeds and set them cut side up in a baking dish.
Brown the turkey with the diced onion until no pink remains (165°F). Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt.
Stir in the rice, tomatoes and beans.
Fill the peppers, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover, top with the cheese and bake for 10 minutes more.

recipes.name: Garlic butter salmon with asparagus and potatoes
recipes.nutrition: ~590 cal, 40 g protein, 34 g carbs, 31 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes with the oil and salt on a sheet pan. Roast for 20 minutes.
Melt the butter with the minced garlic and lemon juice.
Push the potatoes aside and add the salmon and asparagus. Spoon the garlic butter over them.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes until the salmon flakes easily (145°F).

recipes.name: Bean and veggie quesadillas
recipes.nutrition: ~600 cal, 36 g protein, 70 g carbs, 20 g fat
steps: Cook the sliced pepper and onion in the oil for 4 minutes. Add the spinach, cumin and a pinch of salt until wilted.
Mash half the beans with a fork and stir in the rest.
Spread the beans over half of each tortilla. Top with the vegetables and cheese, and fold.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side until crisp and melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa and yogurt.

recipes.name: Chicken sausage, pepper and potato skillet
recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 36 g protein, 40 g carbs, 24 g fat
steps: Cook the potatoes in the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until golden and tender.
Add the sliced peppers and onion, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the sliced sausage and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until browned and hot through (165°F).
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set.

recipes.name: Chickpea shakshuka
recipes.nutrition: ~630 cal, 33 g protein, 68 g carbs, 25 g fat
steps: Cook the diced onion and pepper in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, 1/2 cup of water and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Make 4 wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set.
Top with feta and cilantro. Serve with toast.

recipes.name: Red lentil soup
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 29 g protein, 72 g carbs, 5 g fat
steps: Cook the diced onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and broth. Simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils fall apart.
Stir in the spinach, lemon juice and salt. Blend part of it if you like it smoother.
Serve with a spoon of yogurt and toast.

recipes.name: Chicken tortilla soup
recipes.nutrition: ~430 cal, 40 g protein, 47 g carbs, 11 g fat
steps: Simmer the chicken in the broth with the diced onion, garlic, jalapeño, cumin and chili powder for 15 minutes, until 165°F.
Lift the chicken out and shred it with two forks.
Add the tomatoes, beans and corn. Simmer for 10 minutes. Return the chicken and season with salt and lime.
Cut the tortillas into strips and toast them in a 400°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp.
Top the bowls with tortilla strips, avocado and cilantro.

recipes.name: Minestrone with white beans
recipes.nutrition: ~430 cal, 22 g protein, 72 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Cook the diced onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, diced zucchini and Italian seasoning for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and broth and bring to a boil. Add the pasta and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the beans and spinach until hot. Salt to taste.
Serve with the parmesan.

recipes.name: Hummus and veggie sticks
recipes.nutrition: ~180 cal, 8 g protein, 28 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Cut the carrots and cucumber into sticks.
Dip.

recipes.name: Apple and peanut butter
recipes.nutrition: ~280 cal, 8 g protein, 32 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Slice the apple.
Spread or dip with the peanut butter.

recipes.name: Hard-boiled eggs
recipes.nutrition: ~140 cal, 13 g protein, 1 g carbs, 10 g fat
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes.
Cool in cold water, then peel.
Boil a batch: they keep for a week in the fridge, unpeeled.

recipes.name: Cottage cheese and pineapple
recipes.nutrition: ~180 cal, 19 g protein, 18 g carbs, 4 g fat
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with the pineapple.

recipes.name: Edamame with sea salt
recipes.nutrition: ~190 cal, 18 g protein, 14 g carbs, 8 g fat
steps: Microwave or boil the edamame for 3 minutes.
Drain and sprinkle with salt.

recipes.name: Chicken congee with ginger (Chinese rice porridge)

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: jasmine or any white rice, rinsed

recipes.nutrition: ~390 cal, 40 g protein, 30 g carbs, 11 g fat
steps: Put the rice, broth, ginger and garlic in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add the whole chicken breasts, turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift the chicken out and shred it with two forks. Keep simmering the rice for 25 to 30 minutes more, stirring often, until it breaks down into a creamy porridge.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
Stir the chicken back in with the soy sauce, salt and white pepper. Add hot water if it is too thick.
Top each bowl with a halved egg, sliced scallions and a few drops of sesame oil. It thickens in the fridge; loosen it with water when you reheat it.
recipes.volumeTip: Stir a bag of baby spinach into the pot for the last minute.

recipes.name: Masala omelet with toast (Indian)
recipes.nutrition: ~440 cal, 29 g protein, 35 g carbs, 21 g fat
steps: Beat the eggs with the turmeric, cayenne and a pinch of salt. Stir in the onion, tomato, spinach, chili and chopped cilantro.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg mixture and spread the vegetables out evenly.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top is nearly set. Flip or fold it and cook for 1 minute more.
Serve with the toast.

recipes.name: Tortang talong with rice (Filipino eggplant omelet)

ingredients.name: eggplant
ingredients.note: halved lengthwise; or 2 long Asian eggplants, left whole

recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 20 g protein, 57 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Heat the broiler. Prick the eggplant, set it cut side down on a lined pan and broil for 15 to 20 minutes until the skin is charred and the flesh is very soft.
When it is cool enough to handle, peel off the skin, leaving the stem on. Press each half flat with a fork.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper in a shallow dish. Lay one eggplant half in the egg and spoon egg over it to coat it well.
Heat half the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Slide in the eggplant, pour over half of the egg left in the dish and cook for 3 minutes a side until golden and set. Repeat with the other half.
Dice the tomatoes and onion and toss with a pinch of salt.
Serve the omelets with the rice, the tomato salad and the soy sauce mixed with lime juice for dipping.

recipes.name: Broiled salmon, rice and miso soup (Japanese breakfast)
recipes.servingSize: 1 fillet, 1/2 cup rice and 1 cup soup
recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 45 g protein, 32 g carbs, 26 g fat
steps: Heat the broiler. Pat the salmon dry, sprinkle both sides with salt and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Slice the cucumber thinly and toss it with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Broil the salmon skin side down on a lined pan for 7 to 9 minutes until it flakes easily (145°F).
Bring 2 cups of water to a simmer. Add the tofu and spinach, cook for 1 minute and turn off the heat.
Stir the miso with a ladle of the hot water in a small bowl until smooth, then stir it into the pot. Do not boil it again.
Serve the salmon with the warm rice, the cucumber and a bowl of soup topped with sliced scallions.

recipes.name: Banh mi op la (Vietnamese fried eggs with baguette)
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 25 g protein, 62 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Toss the carrot with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Leave it for 10 minutes to pickle lightly.
Warm the baguette in a 350°F oven or a toaster for 3 to 4 minutes until the crust is crisp.
Heat the oil in a small nonstick pan over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Sprinkle the eggs with the soy sauce and plenty of black pepper.
Serve with the baguette, cucumber, tomato, jalapeño, pickled carrot and cilantro, dipping the bread in the yolks.

recipes.name: Vegetable dalia (Indian cracked-wheat porridge)

ingredients.name: bulgur
ingredients.note: coarse; the supermarket stand-in for dalia

recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 26 g protein, 64 g carbs, 13 g fat
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Stir the cumin and peanuts for 1 minute, then add the onion, ginger and chili and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the carrot, tomato, turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the bulgur and toast it for 1 minute.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the peas, cover again and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until the bulgur is tender and the water is absorbed.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, scatter with cilantro and serve with the yogurt on the side.

recipes.name: Goi ga (Vietnamese chicken and cabbage salad)
recipes.nutrition: ~420 cal, 45 g protein, 38 g carbs, 9 g fat
steps: Simmer the chicken in salted water to cover for 15 to 18 minutes until it reaches 165°F. Cool it for a few minutes, then shred it with two forks.
Whisk the fish sauce, the juice of both limes, the sugar, vinegar, garlic and chili until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the onion in the dressing and let it sit for 5 minutes to soften.
Add the cabbage, carrots, chicken and roughly chopped mint and cilantro. Toss well.
Top with the peanuts and serve with the rice.
For meal prep, keep the dressing and peanuts separate. The undressed salad keeps for 3 days.

recipes.name: Rajma chawal (Indian kidney bean curry with rice)
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 21 g protein, 80 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, turmeric and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until thick.
Add the beans and 1 1/2 cups of water. Simmer for 20 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce. Stir in the garam masala.
Stir the cucumber into the yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Serve the beans over the rice with cilantro and the cucumber yogurt. Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

recipes.name: Dal bhat with spinach (Nepali lentils and rice)
recipes.servingSize: 1 cup dal with 3/4 cup rice and greens
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 21 g protein, 76 g carbs, 8 g fat
steps: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric, tomato and 4 1/2 cups of water for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and soupy. Add 1 tsp salt.
Heat half the oil in a small pan. Cook the cumin for 30 seconds, then the onion for 6 minutes until golden. Add the ginger and half the garlic for 1 minute.
Scrape the onion mixture into the lentils and simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large pan. Cook the remaining garlic and the red pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then add the spinach and a pinch of salt and stir until wilted.
Serve the dal over the rice with the greens, a squeeze of lemon and cilantro. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Bibimbap with vegetables and egg (Korean rice bowl)
recipes.nutrition: ~570 cal, 29 g protein, 65 g carbs, 24 g fat
steps: Stir the gochujang, half the sesame oil, the honey, vinegar and 1 tbsp of water into a sauce.
Wilt the spinach in a large nonstick pan with a splash of water for 1 minute. Squeeze out the liquid and toss it with the soy sauce, garlic and the rest of the sesame oil.
Wipe the pan. Stir-fry the carrots, zucchini, mushrooms and bean sprouts one at a time in a little of the oil with a pinch of salt, 1 to 2 minutes each. Keep them in separate piles.
Brown the tofu in the same pan for 3 minutes a side. Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Divide the rice between 2 bowls. Arrange the vegetables and tofu on top, add an egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Add the sauce and mix everything together before eating.

recipes.name: Turkey larb lettuce cups (Lao and Thai herb salad)

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: jasmine; 2 tbsp of it is toasted for the salad

recipes.nutrition: ~370 cal, 27 g protein, 45 g carbs, 9 g fat
steps: Toast 2 tbsp of the dry rice in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until deep golden. Cool it, then crush it to a coarse powder in a bag with a rolling pin. Cook the rest of the rice.
Cook the turkey in a pan with 1/4 cup of water over medium-high heat, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes until no pink remains (165°F). Take it off the heat.
Stir in the fish sauce, the juice of both limes, the sugar, red pepper flakes and shallots. Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Fold in the toasted rice powder and the chopped mint, cilantro and scallions. Taste it: it should be sour, salty and a little hot.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and serve with the rice and cucumber.

swaps.label: Ground chicken
swaps.note: The traditional choice (larb gai). Cook to 165°F.

recipes.name: Gado-gado (Indonesian salad with peanut sauce)
recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 28 g protein, 45 g carbs, 24 g fat
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
In the same water, boil the eggs for 10 minutes. Add the green beans and cabbage for the last 3 minutes and the bean sprouts for the last 30 seconds. Drain, then cool and peel the eggs.
Pat the tofu dry, cube it and brown it in the oil in a nonstick pan for 6 to 8 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, garlic and sriracha with 1/3 cup of warm water until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, halved eggs and cucumber on plates and spoon over the peanut sauce.
For meal prep, pack the sauce separately. It all keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Liang mian with chicken (Chinese cold sesame noodles)

ingredients.name: tahini
ingredients.note: stands in for Chinese sesame paste

recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 39 g protein, 55 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Simmer the chicken in water to cover for 15 to 18 minutes until it reaches 165°F. Cool it, then shred it with two forks.
Boil the spaghetti as the packet says. Drain, rinse under cold water until cool and toss with the sesame oil.
Whisk the tahini, peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, garlic and ginger with 3 to 4 tbsp of warm water until smooth and pourable. Add sriracha to taste.
Toss the noodles with the sauce. Top with the chicken, cucumbers, carrots, sliced scallions and sesame seeds.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Loosen it with a splash of water before eating.
recipes.volumeTip: Toss in a few handfuls of shredded cabbage or bean sprouts.

recipes.name: Yam tuna with rice (Thai tuna salad)
recipes.nutrition: ~400 cal, 36 g protein, 52 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Whisk the juice of both limes with the fish sauce, sugar, chili and lemongrass paste in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the shallots, celery, tomatoes and cucumber and toss.
Fold in the tuna gently, keeping it in chunks, with the torn mint, cilantro and sliced scallions.
Serve over lettuce leaves with the rice, topped with the peanuts.

recipes.name: Dubu jorim with rice (Korean braised tofu)
recipes.nutrition: ~470 cal, 28 g protein, 49 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Cut the tofu into 1/2-inch slices and pat them very dry with paper towels.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar, gochugaru, garlic, half the scallions and 1/2 cup of water into a sauce.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Brown the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes a side, in two batches if needed.
Return all the tofu to the pan with the onion. Pour over the sauce and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, spooning the sauce over the tofu, until it has reduced by half.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Drizzle the tofu with the sesame oil and scatter with sesame seeds and the rest of the scallions. Serve with the rice and broccoli. Keeps 4 days and is good cold.

recipes.name: Chicken adobo with rice (Filipino)

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: whole peppercorns if you have them

recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 51 g protein, 46 g carbs, 17 g fat
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat for 3 minutes a side.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, pepper, brown sugar and 1/2 cup of water. Bring to a boil without stirring.
Turn the heat down, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, turning the chicken once, until it reaches 165°F.
Uncover and boil for 5 to 8 minutes until the sauce is reduced and glossy.
Steam the green beans for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the sauce spooned over and the beans on the side.

recipes.name: Kung pao chicken with rice (Sichuan)
recipes.nutrition: ~520 cal, 47 g protein, 47 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and 1 tsp of the cornstarch.
Whisk the rest of the soy sauce and cornstarch with the vinegar, sugar and 1/4 cup of water.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and 165°F inside. Set it aside.
Stir-fry the peppers and zucchini for 3 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, red pepper flakes and scallion whites for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy. Stir in the peanuts, sesame oil and scallion greens.
Serve over the rice.

swaps.label: Tofu
swaps.note: Pat the tofu dry and brown it for 6 to 8 minutes before the vegetables.

recipes.name: Chicken satay with peanut sauce (Malaysian)
recipes.servingSize: 3 skewers with 1/2 cup rice and salad
recipes.nutrition: ~470 cal, 46 g protein, 36 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, the turmeric, coriander, cumin, lemongrass paste, half the garlic, half the brown sugar and the oil. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the rest of the soy sauce, garlic and brown sugar, the lime juice, sriracha and 1/3 cup of warm water until smooth.
Slice the cucumbers and onion and toss with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Thread the chicken onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water first). Grill or broil on high for 4 to 5 minutes a side until lightly charred and 165°F inside.
Serve the skewers with the peanut sauce, cucumber salad and rice.

recipes.name: Dak galbi (Korean spicy chicken with cabbage)

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 40 g protein, 66 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, gochugaru, garlic, ginger and sesame oil together. Toss the chicken in half of it and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the sweet potatoes and onion for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the cabbage, the rest of the sauce and 1/4 cup of water.
Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Uncover and cook for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce. Top with sliced scallions and sesame seeds and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Keema matar (Pakistani ground beef with peas)
recipes.servingSize: 1 cup keema with half a naan and salad
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 34 g protein, 44 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Cook the diced onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes until no pink remains (160°F). Drain off extra fat.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne and 1 tsp salt for 1 minute. Add the canned tomatoes and yogurt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Add the peas and garam masala and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the peas are hot.
Dice the cucumber, fresh tomatoes and red onion and toss with lemon juice and salt.
Scatter the keema with cilantro and serve with warm naan and the salad.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Cook to 165°F.

recipes.name: Bo luc lac (Vietnamese shaking beef) with rice
recipes.servingSize: 1 cup beef on salad with 3/4 cup rice
recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 41 g protein, 43 g carbs, 15 g fat
steps: Toss the beef with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, half the sugar, the garlic and the black pepper. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Slice half the onion thinly and toss it with the vinegar, the rest of the sugar and a pinch of salt. Cut the other half into wedges.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan over high heat until very hot. Sear the beef in a single layer for 1 minute without moving it, in two batches. Return it all to the pan.
Add the onion wedges and shake the pan for 2 to 3 minutes until the beef is browned and 145°F inside.
Pile the arugula and tomatoes on a platter and top with the beef, its juices and the pickled onion.
Serve with the rice and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Char siu pork tenderloin with bok choy (Cantonese)
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 43 g protein, 52 g carbs, 8 g fat
steps: Stir the hoisin, soy sauce, honey, five-spice, garlic and ginger together. Set aside 2 tbsp for serving. Coat the pork with the rest and marinate for 30 minutes (or overnight).
Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the pork on a rack over a foil-lined pan.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning it and brushing with the marinade left in the dish halfway through, until it reaches 145°F. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Steam or boil the bok choy for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender. Drain and toss with the sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Serve the pork over the rice with the bok choy, the reserved sauce and sliced scallions.

recipes.name: Miso-glazed cod with sesame spinach (Japanese)
recipes.nutrition: ~390 cal, 39 g protein, 47 g carbs, 5 g fat
steps: Stir the miso, honey, vinegar and 1 tsp of water into a smooth paste. Pat the cod dry, coat the tops with the paste and let it sit for 15 minutes (or up to a day in the fridge).
Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Line a pan with foil and spray it lightly.
Broil the cod for 7 to 9 minutes until the glaze is browned in spots and the fish flakes easily (145°F).
Wilt the spinach in a pot of boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain, rinse with cold water and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Toss the spinach with the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and sesame seeds.
Serve the cod with the rice and spinach, topped with sliced scallions.

recipes.name: Pad thai with shrimp (Thai stir-fried rice noodles)

ingredients.name: limes
ingredients.note: the juice stands in for tamarind

recipes.nutrition: ~510 cal, 35 g protein, 61 g carbs, 15 g fat
steps: Soak the noodles in hot tap water for 20 to 25 minutes until bendy but still firm, then drain.
Stir the fish sauce, brown sugar, the juice of 1 lime, the vinegar and 2 tbsp of water until the sugar dissolves.
Heat half the oil in a wok or large nonstick pan over high heat. Cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and the shallot for 30 seconds. Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Push the noodles aside, scramble the eggs in the space, then toss them through.
Return the shrimp with the scallions and most of the bean sprouts and toss for 1 minute.
Top with the peanuts, the rest of the sprouts, cilantro and wedges of the second lime.
recipes.volumeTip: Toss in a shredded carrot and an extra cup of bean sprouts with the scallions.

swaps.label: Chicken breast
swaps.note: Stir-fry for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains (165°F).

recipes.name: Kiri malu (Sri Lankan coconut fish curry) with rice

ingredients.name: white fish fillets
ingredients.note: such as cod or tilapia, cut into large chunks

recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 38 g protein, 48 g carbs, 11 g fat
steps: Toss the fish with half the turmeric, half the lime juice and 1/2 tsp salt.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, chili, cinnamon stick, curry powder and the rest of the turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, green beans, coconut milk and 1/2 cup of water. Simmer for 8 minutes until the beans are nearly tender.
Slide in the fish in a single layer. Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring as little as you can, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (145°F).
Add salt and the rest of the lime juice to taste. Serve over the rice.

recipes.name: Palak paneer with rice (Indian spinach and cheese curry)
recipes.nutrition: ~440 cal, 22 g protein, 49 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: Brown the paneer in half the oil in a nonstick pan for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden. Set aside.
Cook the onion in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until soft. Add the spinach and 1/2 cup of water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend with a stick blender (or in a blender) until mostly smooth, then return it to the pan.
Take the pan off the heat for a minute, then stir in the yogurt and garam masala. Fold in the paneer and warm through gently without boiling.
Serve over the rice.

swaps.label: Chicken breast
swaps.note: Brown for 6 to 8 minutes until 165°F. This makes chicken saag.

recipes.name: Anda curry with rice (Indian egg curry)
recipes.servingSize: 2 eggs in sauce with 3/4 cup rice
recipes.nutrition: ~400 cal, 19 g protein, 50 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes. Cool them in cold water, peel them and cut a few shallow slits in each.
Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, paprika and turmeric for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes, tomato paste, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup of water. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Add the peas and eggs, spoon the sauce over them and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the garam masala.
Serve over the rice with cilantro.
recipes.volumeTip: Wilt a bag of baby spinach into the sauce with the peas.

recipes.name: Pho ga (Vietnamese chicken noodle soup)

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: Thai basil if you can find it

recipes.nutrition: ~470 cal, 49 g protein, 55 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Char the onion and ginger, cut side down, in a dry pot over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until blackened in spots.
Add the star anise, cinnamon stick, cloves and coriander and toast for 30 seconds. Pour in the broth and 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken, turn the heat to low and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes until it reaches 165°F. Lift it out and shred or slice it.
Simmer the broth for 10 minutes more, then strain out the solids. Season with the fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, drain and divide among 4 bowls with the chicken.
Ladle over the boiling broth. Top with the bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, sliced scallions, jalapeño and lime.
For meal prep, store the broth, chicken and noodles separately for up to 4 days.

recipes.name: Tom yum goong (Thai hot and sour shrimp soup)
recipes.nutrition: ~360 cal, 44 g protein, 42 g carbs, 2 g fat
steps: Bring the broth to a boil with the lemongrass paste, ginger, a few strips of lime zest, the chilies and the onion. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque. Take the pot off the heat.
Stir in the fish sauce, sugar and the juice of the limes. Taste it: it should be sour, salty and hot. Add more lime or fish sauce if it needs it.
Ladle over the rice, or serve the rice on the side, and top with cilantro.

recipes.name: Kimchi jjigae (Korean kimchi stew with pork and tofu)

ingredients.name: kimchi
ingredients.note: chopped, with its juice; older and sour is best

recipes.nutrition: ~400 cal, 36 g protein, 36 g carbs, 13 g fat
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the pork for 2 to 3 minutes until it loses its pink color.
Add the kimchi and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the kimchi softens.
Add the onion, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, any kimchi juice and the broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and tofu and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes more. The pork should be at least 145°F.
Top with sliced scallions and serve with the rice. It tastes even better the next day and keeps 4 days in the fridge.

swaps.label: Canned tuna
swaps.note: A classic version (chamchi kimchi jjigae). Skip the first step and add the tuna with the tofu.

recipes.name: Suan la tang (Chinese hot and sour soup with tofu)

ingredients.name: mushrooms
ingredients.note: sliced; shiitake if you can find them

recipes.nutrition: ~410 cal, 35 g protein, 24 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: Bring the broth to a boil with the ginger. Add the mushrooms, carrot and cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and soy sauce and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch with 3 tbsp of cold water, pour it in while stirring and simmer for 1 minute until the soup thickens slightly.
Turn the heat to low. Pour in the eggs in a thin stream while stirring slowly, so they set in ribbons.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vinegar, white pepper and sesame oil. Taste it: add more vinegar for sour or more pepper for heat. Top with sliced scallions.

recipes.name: Mango lassi (Indian yogurt drink)
recipes.nutrition: ~280 cal, 24 g protein, 44 g carbs, 3 g fat
steps: Blend the yogurt, milk, mango, honey and cardamom until smooth.
Add a splash of water if it is too thick, and pour into a glass.

recipes.name: Chana chaat (Indian chickpea salad)
recipes.nutrition: ~230 cal, 12 g protein, 40 g carbs, 4 g fat
steps: Toss the chickpeas with the tomato, cucumber, onion, jalapeño and chopped cilantro.
Season with the lemon juice, cumin, cayenne and salt.
Eat right away or chill. It keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Tuna onigiri (Japanese rice balls)

ingredients.name: cooked rice
ingredients.note: warm; short-grain or sushi rice sticks best

recipes.nutrition: ~250 cal, 16 g protein, 35 g carbs, 4 g fat
steps: Mix the tuna with the mayo.
Wet your hands and rub them with a pinch of salt. Flatten a quarter of the rice in your palm, add a spoonful of tuna and press the rice around it into a ball or triangle.
Make 4 in all and wrap a strip of nori around each. Wrap them in plastic for later and eat them the same day.

recipes.name: Çılbır: poached eggs on garlic yogurt with toast (Turkish)
recipes.servingSize: 2 eggs on yogurt with 2 slices of toast

ingredients.name: red pepper flakes
ingredients.note: Aleppo pepper if you have it

recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 39 g protein, 36 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Stir the grated garlic and a pinch of salt into the yogurt and spread it in a shallow bowl. Let it lose its chill while you cook.
Bring a small pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack in the eggs and poach for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set.
Melt the butter in a small pan, then stir in the paprika and red pepper flakes for 20 seconds until it smells toasty.
Lift the eggs onto the yogurt with a slotted spoon, spoon the spiced butter over them and scatter with dill.
Serve with the toast for scooping.
recipes.volumeTip: Add sliced cucumber and tomato on the side, as on a Turkish breakfast table.

recipes.name: Fatteh: chickpeas with garlic yogurt and pita (Lebanese)
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 28 g protein, 59 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Tear the pita into bite-size pieces, toss with 1 tsp of the oil and bake for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in their liquid with the cumin for 5 minutes, then drain, keeping 2 tbsp of the liquid.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, the saved liquid and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in the rest of the oil over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Layer the pita chips, warm chickpeas and yogurt sauce in two bowls. Top with the pine nuts, paprika and parsley and eat right away.

recipes.name: Bircher muesli with apple and walnuts (Swiss)
recipes.nutrition: ~500 cal, 24 g protein, 86 g carbs, 10 g fat
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, raisins, lemon juice and cinnamon together in a bowl or two jars.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 2 hours, so the oats soften.
In the morning, grate the apples and stir them in. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
Top with the walnuts, berries and honey. Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Bauernfrühstück: potato, ham and egg skillet (German)

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: boiled and cooled; leftovers are ideal

recipes.nutrition: ~430 cal, 27 g protein, 40 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: If the potatoes are raw, boil them whole for 15 to 20 minutes until just tender, then cool. Cut them into thin slices.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the potatoes for 8 to 10 minutes, turning now and then, until golden.
Add the onion and ham and cook for 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper and half the chopped chives. Pour over the potatoes, turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the eggs are set (160°F).
Slide onto plates, scatter with the rest of the chives and serve with the tomatoes and pickles.

recipes.name: Kedgeree: curried rice with cod and eggs (British)

ingredients.name: cod fillets
ingredients.note: smoked haddock is traditional if you can find it

recipes.nutrition: ~400 cal, 32 g protein, 45 g carbs, 9 g fat
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel and cut into quarters.
Put the cod in a wide pan with the bay leaves and 2 1/2 cups of water. Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes until it flakes easily (145°F). Lift the fish out and pour the liquid into a jug.
In the same pan, melt the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the rice and 2 cups of the saved liquid. Cover and cook on low for 12 to 15 minutes until the rice is tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Flake the cod into the rice with a fork. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Top with the eggs and chopped parsley. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
recipes.volumeTip: Stir in a few handfuls of baby spinach with the peas.

recipes.name: Kuku sabzi: herb frittata with yogurt (Persian)
recipes.servingSize: 1 wedge with yogurt and half a pita
recipes.nutrition: ~380 cal, 24 g protein, 24 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Finely chop the parsley, cilantro, dill, scallions and spinach; you want about 4 packed cups.
Beat the eggs with the flour, baking powder, turmeric, 3/4 tsp salt and some pepper. Fold in the herbs and walnuts.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch ovenproof nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour in the mixture, smooth the top and cook for 3 minutes to set the bottom.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until firm in the middle.
Cut into 4 wedges. Serve warm or cold with the yogurt and warm pita. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Chicken souvlaki pitas with tzatziki (Greek)
recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 52 g protein, 43 g carbs, 13 g fat
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 1/2 tbsp of the oil, the juice of half the lemon, 2 minced garlic cloves, the oregano, salt and pepper. Marinate for 20 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.

For the tzatziki, grate half the cucumber and squeeze it dry in a clean towel. Stir it into the yogurt with the last garlic clove (grated), the rest of the oil, chopped dill, a squeeze of lemon and salt.
Thread the chicken onto skewers. Grill or broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and 165°F inside. (Or cook it loose in a hot pan.)
Slice the tomatoes, the onion and the rest of the cucumber. Warm the pitas.
Fill each pita with chicken, vegetables and a big spoon of tzatziki. For meal prep, pack the chicken, vegetables and tzatziki separately; they keep 4 days.
recipes.volumeTip: Add shredded romaine to each pita, or skip the pita and serve everything over a big salad.

swaps.label: Halloumi
swaps.note: Skip the salt. Grill or pan-fry the slices for 2 minutes a side until golden.

recipes.name: Salade niçoise with tuna, egg and potatoes (French)
recipes.nutrition: ~530 cal, 40 g protein, 45 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Add the green beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain and cool both under cold water.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the potatoes and green beans in half the dressing.
Arrange the greens on two plates. Top with the potatoes, beans, tomatoes, tuna in big chunks, eggs, olives and capers, and spoon over the rest of the dressing.

recipes.name: Koshari: lentils, rice and pasta in tomato sauce (Egyptian)
recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 18 g protein, 80 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Cook the onions in 1 1/2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown. Set aside.
Simmer the lentils in 4 cups of water for 10 minutes. Add the rice, 1 tsp of the cumin and 1 tsp salt, cover and cook on low for 15 to 18 minutes until both are tender and the water is absorbed.
Boil the pasta as the packet says, then drain.

For the sauce, cook the minced garlic in the rest of the oil for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes, coriander, the rest of the cumin, the red pepper flakes, vinegar and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir the chickpeas into the sauce for the last 5 minutes.
Layer the lentils and rice, the pasta and the sauce in bowls, and top with the browned onions. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; pack the sauce separately.
recipes.volumeTip: Serve with a chopped cucumber and tomato salad on the side.

recipes.name: Sabich: roasted eggplant, egg and hummus pitas (Israeli)
recipes.nutrition: ~450 cal, 18 g protein, 54 g carbs, 21 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the eggplant rounds with the oil, sprinkle with salt and the cumin, and roast on a lined sheet pan for 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumber and toss with chopped parsley, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Stir the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice and 2 tbsp of water until pourable.
Warm the pitas and cut a pocket in each. Spread with hummus, then fill with eggplant, egg, salad and pickles. Drizzle with the tahini sauce and add hot sauce if you like.

recipes.name: Salade de lentilles: lentil salad with goat cheese (French)

ingredients.name: green lentils
ingredients.note: French green (du Puy) hold their shape best

recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 26 g protein, 50 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Put the lentils, bay leaf and thyme in a pot with 5 cups of water. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until tender but not mushy, adding the carrots and celery for the last 5 minutes.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard, shallot, 3/4 tsp salt and some pepper in a large bowl.
Drain the lentils well and take out the bay leaf and thyme. Toss the lentils in the dressing while still warm so they soak it up.
Stir in chopped parsley. Taste and add more salt or vinegar.
Serve warm or cold over the arugula, topped with the goat cheese and walnuts. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add the arugula when serving.

recipes.name: Jollof rice with chicken (Nigerian)

ingredients.name: rice
ingredients.note: long-grain, parboiled if you have it, rinsed

ingredients.name: cayenne
ingredients.note: or half a habanero, blended into the sauce

recipes.nutrition: ~580 cal, 41 g protein, 63 g carbs, 17 g fat
steps: Blend the tomatoes, bell peppers, half the onion, the garlic and ginger until smooth.
Season the chicken with salt, 1 tsp of the curry powder and half the thyme. Brown it in 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pot for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then set aside.

Slice the rest of the onion and cook it in the rest of the oil for 4 minutes. Fry the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then add the blended sauce, the remaining spices, the bay leaves and 1 tsp salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice and broth and set the chicken on top. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 to 30 minutes, without stirring, until the rice is tender and the chicken is 165°F.
Rest for 5 minutes with the lid on, then fluff with a fork. Serve with the cucumber. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
recipes.volumeTip: Serve with steamed green beans or a simple cabbage and carrot slaw.

swaps.label: Shrimp
swaps.note: Skip the browning. Push the shrimp into the rice for the last 5 minutes, until pink and opaque.

recipes.name: Red red: black-eyed pea stew with baked plantains (Ghanaian)

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: gives the color that red palm oil would

recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 22 g protein, 98 g carbs, 10 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Peel the plantains and slice them on the diagonal. Toss with 1/2 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of salt and bake on a lined sheet pan for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Cook the onion in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, smoked paprika and cayenne for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the tomatoes. Simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Add the black-eyed peas and broth. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing some of the peas against the side of the pot so the stew turns creamy. Salt to taste.
Serve the stew with the baked plantains. The stew keeps 4 days in the fridge.
recipes.volumeTip: Stir a few handfuls of baby spinach into the stew at the end.

recipes.name: Smørrebrød: open rye sandwiches with egg and shrimp (Danish)

ingredients.name: rye bread
ingredients.note: dense, dark rye if you can find it

recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 45 g protein, 38 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Simmer the shrimp in salted water for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque. Drain and cool under cold water.
Stir the yogurt, mayo, chopped dill, a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper together.
Lay a lettuce leaf on each slice of bread. Add the cucumber and egg slices, then pile on the shrimp.
Top with a spoon of the dill sauce, more dill and black pepper. Serve with lemon wedges and eat with a knife and fork.

recipes.name: Beef köfte with bulgur pilaf and shepherd's salad (Turkish)
recipes.nutrition: ~500 cal, 39 g protein, 39 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Mix the beef with the grated onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, half the chopped parsley, the cumin, paprika, red pepper flakes, 3/4 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 12 small oval patties.
For the pilaf, cook the diced onion in 1 tbsp of the oil for 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and bulgur, add the broth, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes. Rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Grill, broil or pan-fry the köfte for 4 to 5 minutes a side until browned and 160°F inside.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumbers. Toss with the rest of the parsley, oil and garlic (minced), the lemon juice, sumac and salt.
Serve the köfte with the pilaf, salad and a spoon of yogurt. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; pack the salad separately.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Cook to 165°F.

recipes.name: Chicken cacciatore with soft polenta (Italian)
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 42 g protein, 43 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Brown it in the oil in a wide, deep pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion, peppers and mushrooms for 6 to 8 minutes until soft. Add the minced garlic and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, vinegar, rosemary, olives and capers. Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and 165°F.
Meanwhile, bring 4 cups of water and 1 tsp salt to a boil. Whisk in the cornmeal in a thin stream, then cook on low for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Stir in the parmesan.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over the polenta and finish with torn basil.

recipes.name: Pasta con le sarde: sardine and fennel spaghetti (Sicilian)

ingredients.name: sardines
ingredients.note: in olive oil or water, drained

recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 27 g protein, 56 g carbs, 19 g fat
steps: Toast the panko in 1 tsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Tip it into a bowl.
Boil the spaghetti as the packet says. Save 1 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
While it cooks, soften the fennel and onion in the rest of the oil for 8 to 10 minutes. Add the minced garlic, raisins, pine nuts, red pepper flakes and saffron for 1 minute.
Add the sardines, breaking them into big pieces, and 1/2 cup of the pasta water. Simmer for 2 minutes until the sardines are hot.
Toss in the spaghetti with the lemon juice, adding more pasta water if it looks dry. Salt to taste.
Serve topped with the toasted panko, chopped fennel fronds and parsley.
recipes.volumeTip: Toss in a few handfuls of baby spinach with the spaghetti.

recipes.name: Tortilla española: potato omelet with tomato salad (Spanish)
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 21 g protein, 54 g carbs, 21 g fat
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes, onion and 1 tsp salt, cover and cook for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender but not browned.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl with some pepper. Stir in the hot potatoes and onion and let the mixture sit for 5 minutes.
Wipe the skillet, heat 1/2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat and pour in the mixture. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pan now and then, until the edges are set.
Put a large plate over the skillet, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide it back in. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until just set in the middle.
Toss the greens, sliced tomatoes and roasted peppers with the rest of the oil, the vinegar and salt.
Cut the tortilla into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature with the salad and bread.

recipes.name: Arista: rosemary-garlic pork with white beans (Tuscan)
recipes.servingSize: a quarter of the pork with beans and greens

ingredients.name: sage
ingredients.note: a few leaves, or 1/2 tsp dried

recipes.nutrition: ~510 cal, 51 g protein, 45 g carbs, 14 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix 3 minced garlic cloves with the rosemary, fennel seeds, 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Rub it all over the pork.
Sear the pork in an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes a side. Move the skillet to the oven and roast for 15 to 18 minutes until 145°F in the middle. Rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil in a pot with the last garlic clove (sliced) and the sage for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, beans and broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir the kale into the beans, cover and cook for 5 minutes until wilted. Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Slice the pork and serve it over the beans and greens with any pan juices.

recipes.name: Baked turkey schnitzel with cucumber-dill salad (Austrian)
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, 42 g protein, 49 g carbs, 11 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the panko with the oil and toast it on a sheet pan for 3 to 4 minutes until golden. Tip into a shallow dish and mix in the paprika.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 18 minutes until tender. Drain and toss with the butter and chopped parsley.
Season the cutlets with salt and pepper. Dust with the flour, dip in the egg, then press into the panko.
Set the cutlets on a rack over the sheet pan (or on parchment), spray lightly with cooking spray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until crisp and 165°F inside.
Toss the cucumbers with 1/2 tsp salt and leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze out the water and stir in the sour cream, vinegar, sugar and chopped dill.
Serve the schnitzel with lemon wedges, the potatoes and the cucumber salad.

recipes.name: Gołąbki: cabbage rolls with beef and rice (Polish)
recipes.nutrition: ~480 cal, 33 g protein, 47 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Cut out the cabbage core. Lower the whole head into a large pot of boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes, peeling off 12 outer leaves with tongs as they soften. Trim the thick rib on each leaf.
Boil the rice for 8 minutes, then drain; it will finish cooking in the rolls. Soften the onion and minced garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Mix the beef, rice, onion, egg, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Put about 1/4 cup on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Chop some of the leftover cabbage and spread it in a baking dish. Pack in the rolls seam side down.
Stir the tomatoes with the broth and 1/2 tsp salt, pour over the rolls and add the bay leaves. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour, until the filling is 160°F.
Serve with the sauce, a spoon of sour cream and chopped dill. They taste even better the next day.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Bake until the filling is 165°F.

recipes.name: Samke harra: baked fish with spicy tahini sauce (Lebanese)
recipes.servingSize: 1 fillet with sauce, rice and salad
recipes.nutrition: ~490 cal, 39 g protein, 47 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cook the rice.

Pat the fish dry and set it in a baking dish lined with parchment. Rub with the cumin, coriander, paprika, 1/2 tsp salt and the juice of half a lemon. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until it flakes easily (145°F).
Cook the garlic, jalapeño and red pepper flakes in the oil for 1 minute. Add most of the cilantro and the walnuts and stir for 1 minute more.
Whisk the tahini with the juice of 1 lemon, 1/3 cup of water and a pinch of salt until smooth. Stir it into the pan and warm gently for 1 to 2 minutes; do not let it boil.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumbers and dress with the last of the lemon juice and salt.
Spoon the sauce over the fish, scatter with the rest of the cilantro and serve with the rice and salad.

recipes.name: Baked falafel plates with tahini sauce (Middle Eastern)
recipes.servingSize: 4 falafel with pita, salad and sauce

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.note: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

recipes.nutrition: ~560 cal, 21 g protein, 85 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Brush the parchment with 1 tbsp of the oil.
Pulse the chickpeas, onion, 3 garlic cloves, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander and 1 tsp salt in a food processor until coarse and crumbly, not smooth. Pulse in the flour and baking powder.
Shape into 16 small patties (wet hands help) and set them on the pan. Brush the tops with the rest of the oil.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, the last garlic clove (grated), 3 to 4 tbsp of water and a pinch of salt until pourable.
Chop the romaine, tomatoes and cucumber. Serve the falafel over the salad with warm pita and the tahini sauce.

recipes.name: Bobotie: curried beef bake with yellow rice (South African)
recipes.servingSize: 1 square with 3/4 cup rice and salad
recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 33 g protein, 61 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Cook the onions in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the minced garlic, curry powder and half the turmeric for 1 minute, then the beef. Brown, breaking it up, until no pink remains (160°F).
Take off the heat. Mix in the mashed bread, raisins, apricot jam, vinegar, almonds, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Press into a 9-inch baking dish coated with cooking spray.
Beat the eggs with the saved milk and a pinch of salt. Pour over the meat and push the bay leaves into the top. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is set and golden.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with the rest of the turmeric and a pinch of salt.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumber and season with salt. Serve the bobotie in squares with the yellow rice and salad.

swaps.label: Ground turkey
swaps.note: Brown until no pink remains (165°F).

recipes.name: Chicken yassa: lemon-onion chicken with rice (Senegalese)
recipes.servingSize: 1 cup chicken and onions with 1 cup rice
recipes.nutrition: ~570 cal, 39 g protein, 60 g carbs, 18 g fat
steps: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Toss with the chicken and onions and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade. Broil or grill it for 4 to 5 minutes a side until browned; it will finish cooking in the sauce.
Lift the onions out of the marinade and cook them in the rest of the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the leftover marinade, broth, carrots, bay leaves, olives and the whole jalapeño. Add the chicken, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until it is 165°F and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the rice.
Take out the bay leaves and jalapeño. Serve the chicken and onions over the rice.

swaps.label: Fish (poisson yassa)
swaps.note: Broil for 3 minutes a side, then simmer in the onions for only 5 minutes, until it flakes easily.

recipes.name: Misir wot: spiced red lentils with collards (Ethiopian)
recipes.servingSize: 1 cup lentils with greens and 3/4 cup rice

ingredients.name: berbere
ingredients.note: or 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp cayenne

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: injera flatbread is traditional if you can find it

recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 25 g protein, 91 g carbs, 8 g fat
steps: Cook the onions in 1 1/2 tbsp of the oil over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add 3 minced garlic cloves and the ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Add the lentils, 4 cups of water and 1 tsp salt. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils break down into a thick stew.
Meanwhile, cook the rice.
Cook the last garlic clove (sliced) in the rest of the oil for 30 seconds. Add the collard greens, 1/2 cup of water and a pinch of salt, cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until tender.
Serve the lentils and greens side by side over the rice.

recipes.name: Chicken tagine with olives and lemon (Moroccan)
recipes.nutrition: ~500 cal, 42 g protein, 46 g carbs, 16 g fat
steps: Toss the chicken with the turmeric, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot for 3 minutes a side, then set aside. Cook the onions in the same pot for 6 minutes, then add the minced garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Return the chicken with the carrots, broth and the zest of the lemon. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini and olives and simmer, uncovered, for 10 minutes more, until the chicken is 165°F and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the lemon juice.
Pour 1 1/4 cups of boiling water over the couscous with a pinch of salt. Cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the tagine over the couscous with chopped cilantro.

recipes.name: Lohikeitto: salmon, potato and leek soup (Finnish)
recipes.servingSize: 2 cups with a slice of rye bread

ingredients.name: leek
ingredients.note: large, white and light green parts, sliced

recipes.nutrition: ~540 cal, 35 g protein, 48 g carbs, 22 g fat
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, broth, bay leaves and allspice. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the salmon and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes until it is opaque and flakes easily (145°F).
Pour in the milk and heat through without boiling. Stir in most of the dill and season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls, top with the rest of the dill and serve with the rye bread. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently.

recipes.name: Caldo verde: kale and potato soup with sausage (Portuguese)

ingredients.name: kale
ingredients.note: stems removed, cut into thin ribbons

recipes.nutrition: ~360 cal, 20 g protein, 43 g carbs, 12 g fat
steps: Brown the kielbasa in the oil in a large pot for 4 to 5 minutes until hot through (165°F). Lift it out and set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and broth. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Mash about half the potatoes in the pot with a potato masher (or blend briefly) so the broth turns creamy.
Stir in the kale and kielbasa and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes until the greens are tender. Season with salt and pepper. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Harira: tomato, lentil and chickpea soup (Moroccan)
recipes.nutrition: ~410 cal, 21 g protein, 68 g carbs, 6 g fat
steps: Cook the onion and celery in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes.
